answer: Coordination Density Pricing.** Each agent identity must occupy a distinct network region, verified by latency triangulation. New identities register onto a sparse knoll of the routing graph, where message delivery costs scale with how densely that neighborhood already coordinates. A Sybil cluster concentrating in one canyon of addresses pays multiplicatively rising relay fees per identity, since dense coordination is priced as the scarce good. An honest agent spreading across a wide island pays near-baseline rates.
